accuracy_how: in-process loglikelihood scoring of the SAME gguf file via llama-cpp-python (llama_cpp.Llama(model_path), n_ctx=2048); lm-eval harness supplies datasets/prompts/metrics (default smoke: arc_easy x50; real audits use hidden validation subset). model is evaluated quantized.
adtc_reference_hardware: 8GB RAM laptop (7GB scoring budget), x86-64 Intel i5 10-12th gen or Ryzen 5 3000-5000, integrated GPU only, 256GB SSD, Ubuntu 22.04

decisions.gate_a: STOP - edge0-style custom multi-file ssd-streaming runtime is not scoreable by the official profiler. no further edge35 runtime work authorized on this branch unless the profiler contract changes (custom entrypoint support) or organizers confirm an alternative scoring path.
decisions.recommended_next: stay on dense-GGUF path (best small-model frontier); optionally revisit only if profiler adds custom-runtime support.

efficiency_memory_answers.peak_vs_steady: peak is max over 100ms samples across the whole llama-bench run (includes load); steady_state (mean of last 60s or last half) also recorded
efficiency_memory_answers.what_counts: psutil rss of profiler process plus all recursive children (llama-bench). anonymous + touched file/mmap pages count; untouched mmap pages and page cache do not.

execution_answers.accuracy_entrypoint: no - profiler loads the gguf itself in-process
execution_answers.are_lora_prerouter_weights_allowed: no - auxiliary weights are never loaded, so they cannot affect the score
execution_answers.are_ssd_resident_aux_files_allowed: no - profiler reads exactly one file; sidecars are ignored
execution_answers.can_runtime_choose_cache_budget: no - no custom code runs at all
execution_answers.cold_vs_warm: not distinguished - one llama-bench run per profile
execution_answers.gguf_required: effectively yes - throughput (llama-bench) and accuracy (llama-cpp-python) both load model_path as gguf; non-gguf aborts the run before any report is written
execution_answers.is_model_load_time_scored: partially - load happens inside the sampled window, so it can raise peak rss; no separate load-time metric
execution_answers.is_only_generation_tps_scored: yes for S_perf (generation row avg_ts); prompt-processing rate is recorded and used only for first_token_latency_ms approximation
execution_answers.is_prompt_processing_included: only via first_token_latency_ms = prompt_tokens/pp_rate (informational, not in S_total)
execution_answers.is_ttft_scored: recorded (first_token_latency_ms) but not part of S_total; compare tolerance +-25%
execution_answers.model_path_resolution: <submission>/_runtime.model_path, default model.gguf; missing file exits code 2
execution_answers.threads: not pinned by profiler (llama-bench default); participant script pins -ngl 0 (cpu-only)

measured_local_baseline.note: repo's previous official self-check (docs/gate1-profiler-run.json) to be compared before any new claims; local rig currently disk-full (317MB free) and cannot download checkpoints.

qa_method: read profiler source at pinned commit (throughput.py, memory.py, accuracy.py, gguf.py, cli.py, comparator.py, schema) + stock model config from huggingface; no profiler code executed locally (accuracy/bench stack not installed, disk full).
questions_1_to_26_summary: 1 GGUF: effectively required (both stages load model_path as GGUF). 2 llama.cpp: effectively required (llama-bench + llama-cpp-python). 3 profiler loads model itself: YES. 4 executes our entrypoint: NO. 5 custom native runtime: NO. 6 multiple weight files: NO. 7 ssd-resident aux files: NO (ignored). 8 lora/prerouter aux weights: NO (never loaded). 9 efficiency = process RSS only: YES. 10 page cache: NOT counted. 11 mmap pages: counted once touched (resident). 12 process-tree RSS: YES. 13 disk usage: NOT measured. 14 peak vs steady: PEAK over run. 15 page-cache flush: NO. 16 repeated prompts/one process: NO, single bench run. 17 cold vs warm: NOT distinguished. 18 load time scored: only via peak RSS. 19 TTFT scored: recorded, not in total. 20 only generation tps: YES. 21 prompt processing: only informational. 22 cpu flags: not pinned by profiler (audit uses scalar build). 23 simd disabled: in audit (scalar llama.cpp). 24 threads: unpinned. 25 context: n_ctx=2048 for accuracy; bench -p 512 -n 128. 26 dynamic cache budget: impossible (no custom code runs).

scoring.S_perf_formula: 100*min(tps_gen/15.0, 1.0) -- fixed 15 tps reference in profiler code (site text says relative-to-fastest; code is what runs)
scoring.fail_bound: delta beyond 50% hard-fails; outside tolerance flags for manual review

throughput_how: spawns llama-bench -m <model.gguf> -p 512 -n 128 -ngl 0 --output json; S_perf uses generation-row avg_ts; thread count unpinned by profiler
